exam_scheme.note: Exam scheme is notified under Advt. No. 9/2024 and corrigendum dated 14.10.2025, updating the criminal law papers to incorporate Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA). Preliminary exam is screening only; final merit is based on Final Examination (1,100 marks) + Personality Test (100 marks) = 1,200 marks total.

stages.source_label: WBPSC — Scheme and Syllabus for West Bengal Judicial Service Examination, 2024 (Advt. No. 9/2024)

papers.paper_name: Law, English & General Knowledge Composite Paper (200 MCQs covering English Composition [30m], GK/Current Affairs/Reasoning [40m], Indian Constitution [20m], Contracts & Torts [20m], BSA [20m], CPC [20m], BNSS & BNS [20m], Personal Law [10m], and Law of Limitation [20m])
papers.negative_marking: Negative marking applies for each wrong answer as per commission rules

stages.source_label: WBPSC — Scheme and Syllabus for West Bengal Judicial Service Examination, 2024 (Advt. No. 9/2024)

papers.paper_name: Compulsory Paper 1: English Composition, Essay and Précis Writing
Compulsory Paper 2: Bengali/Hindi/Urdu/Nepali/Santali Composition, Essay and Translation from English
Compulsory Paper 3: General Knowledge and Current Affairs
Compulsory Paper 5: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)
Compulsory Paper 7: Law of Contracts and Torts
Compulsory Paper 8: Transfer of Property Act

Optional Paper I (Chosen from Hindu Law / Muhammadan Law / Jurisprudence & Principles of Legislation / Indian Law relating to Companies & Insurance / Principles of Equity, Trusts & Specific Relief / Partnership Act / Law of Limitation & Prescription / Constitution & Constitutional Law)
Optional Paper II (Chosen from 8 prescribed optional subjects)
Optional Paper III (Chosen from 8 prescribed optional subjects)

financial_package.note: Judicial officers in West Bengal are compensated under the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) Cadre J-1 pay scale as approved by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India and implemented by the West Bengal Judicial Department.
financial_package.pay_source_label: High Court at Calcutta & Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) Report as approved by Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India
financial_package.estimate_note: Gross salary calculated on Cadre J-1 entry basic pay of ₹77,840 with project constant 58% Dearness Allowance (effective 1 Jul 2025), judicial House Rent Allowance (16% to 24% depending on posting station or government bungalow), sumptuary allowance, and robe allowance. In-hand estimate factors in GPF/NPS contributions and statutory deductions.
official_perks: Official designated residential accommodation (bungalow / government quarter) or Judicial HRA
Official staff car with driver or dedicated conveyance allowance for judicial duties
Sumptuary Allowance and Robe Allowance as prescribed under SNJPC
Comprehensive medical facility and reimbursement for officer and family
Subsidized electricity and domestic water supply allowances
Reimbursement for landline telephone, mobile, and broadband connectivity
Residential peon / home orderly allowance as per judicial service rules

competition_benchmarks.note: Benchmark figures for WBJS 2023 (Advt. No. 19/2023) and WBJS 2022 (Advt. No. 19/2022) are extracted directly from official WBPSC notifications. The 2022 cycle notified 29 vacancies (12 clear, 17 anticipated). The 2024 cycle (Advt. No. 9/2024) Preliminary examination was held on 27.09.2026.
